content.title: About
content.content: Corn syrup is a thick, sweet syrup made from corn starch through hydrolysis. It is widely used in the food industry as a sweetener, stabilizer, and texture enhancer in baked goods, candies, and beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn syrup is often classified as high‑fructose corn syrup (HFCS) when it contains more than 55 % fructose.
It is cheaper than sugar thanks to the abundant production of corn in the United States and other countries.
The syrup can be light (low glucose) or dark (with added caramel for color and flavor).
Its mass adoption in soft drinks during the 1970s contributed to the rise of sugar consumption in the US.
Corn syrup is a common ingredient in barbecue sauces, ketchup, and marinades.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Contains simple sugars that are rapidly absorbed, helping to quickly replenish glycogen stores.

items.title: Improves baked goods texture
items.content: Retains moisture in breads and cakes, keeping them softer and fresher longer.

items.title: Stabilizer in confections
items.content: Prevents sugar crystallization in ice cream and frozen desserts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and metabolic disturbances.

items.title: Fructose load
items.content: Large amounts of fructose may raise blood triglycerides and stress the liver.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to corn‑derived products.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add corn syrup to doughs, sauces, marinades, drinks, ice cream, and confectionery. It works well as a liquid sweetener in recipes that require moisture and softness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. Properly stored, it lasts 12–24 months. Discard if the syrup changes odor, color, or taste.
